idea: A board-game café in a town of about 9,000 people, €4 a table plus drinks

mia.title: Board-game café in a small town
mia.one_liner: A warm place to play, with 300 games and someone to teach them.

brief.concept: A 90 m² café with a 300-game library, €4 table fee plus drinks, open Tuesday to Sunday afternoons and evenings.
brief.for: Friends and couples aged 20 to 40 in town who play at home and have nowhere to go on weeknights.
brief.goal: Sell 40 paid tickets to one games night in a bar before looking at any premises.

checklist.task: Count evening footfall on the main square
checklist.how: Tally people passing 18:00–22:00 on a Tuesday, Friday and Sunday.

checklist.task: Interview 15 people who play board games
checklist.how: Ask where they last played, with whom, and what they spent that evening.
checklist.done_when: 15 logged; 6+ spent money on a night out

checklist.task: Agree a games night with one bar
checklist.how: Offer a Thursday 19:00–23:00 night; the bar keeps drinks, you keep the €8 entry.

checklist.task: Price three empty premises near the square
checklist.how: Ask rent, licence for food and drink, and fit-out needed.
checklist.done_when: Three quotes with rent and licence

checklist.task: Sell tickets for the first games night
checklist.how: Message everyone interviewed and two local groups; ask each to bring a friend.

checklist.task: Run the games night and count
checklist.how: Teach three games, log who came, what they spent, who asks for the next one.
checklist.done_when: Attendance and spend per person logged

checklist.how: Compare tickets sold and spend per head with Sam's break-even.
checklist.done_when: Decision written down with the numbers

leo.headline: The town is too small for a full-time café.
leo.summary: People play at home and would come to a good night, but a town this size fills a games café a few nights a month, not six days a week. It only works as an event, not as premises.

signals.name: Demand
signals.why: A town of ~9,000 gives few regular players

signals.name: Competition gap
signals.why: No games café, but bars already host quiz nights

signals.name: Price acceptance
signals.why: Table fees are unusual; people expect to pay for drinks only

signals.name: Channel
signals.why: Word of mouth works; nothing else reaches players

signals.name: Timing
signals.why: Busy on weekends, quiet Tuesday to Thursday

leo.why_go: What would have to be true: 40+ people paying for a games night every month for three months, in a town with no other evening venue.

risks.risk: Weeknights stay empty while rent runs every day.
risks.mitigation: Test one night a month in a bar; no lease.

risks.risk: Players buy the games and stay home.
risks.mitigation: Count who returns to the second night.

risks.risk: A €4 table fee feels like paying to sit down.

pivot.idea: A monthly games night in an existing bar, €8 entry, no premises.
pivot.why: Fixes demand and price: one full night a month needs 40 players, not 31 every day.

leo.next_step: Run one games night in a bar this month: 40 paid tickets is the bar.

market_facts.fact: Board-game cafés usually rely on a large town or a city centre with a student population.
Table fees in games cafés are commonly €3 to €6 a person.
A games café of about 90 m² typically seats 40 to 50 people.
Bars in small towns often host one themed night a week to fill quiet evenings.

competitors.note: Free, and the games are already there

competitors.note: Cheap, social, one night a week

competitors.name: Games cafés in the nearest city

competitors.note: Always on, but nobody in the room

interviews.who: People in town who own three or more board games
interviews.where: The main square in the evening and two local social groups
questions: When did you last play a board game, and where?
What did you spend that evening?
When did you last travel to play or to a games event?
What stopped you from playing more often last month?
interviews.good_sign: They travelled or paid to play in the last three months and say it unprompted.

kill_criteria: Stop if fewer than 6 of 15 players spent money on a games night last month.
Stop if the first games night sells under 25 tickets.
leo.verdict_rule: Go from 7.0 with no signal at 3 or below · Pivot 5.0–6.9 · No-go under 5.0

confidence.note: Desk estimates only, no web sources: signals capped at 7.5. Interviews decide.

memo.purpose: A board-game café for a town of about 9,000 people.
memo.problem: Players in town have nowhere to play on weeknights except home, and the nearest games café is 40 minutes away.
memo.insight: The demand is real but monthly, not daily. An event fills a room; premises need people every evening.
memo.verdict_line: No-go as a café: it needs 31 visitors a day to break even, and the town gives about 24. Test a monthly games night first.
